vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: cron-limited
Version: 1.1.0

The skill provides utility for managing temporary cron jobs and lunar-to-solar date reminders. It functions by using the `openclaw` CLI to schedule tasks and implements a 'limited repeat' feature by scheduling a secondary one-time task to delete the primary task after a calculated duration. While the script relies on a specific hardcoded path for a Python virtual environment (`/tmp/lunar-venv/`) to handle lunar date conversions, there is no evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or unauthorized command execution beyond the stated purpose in `scripts/cron-limited.sh` and `SKILL.md`.

llm.summary: The skill's code largely matches its described purpose (limited-repeat cron + lunar conversion), but it uses a surprising mechanism—scheduling a future message that contains an actionable openclaw command to delete the main job—which is unexpected and could be misused or behave differently than the author claims.

dimensions.detail: Name/description, declared dependencies (Python + lunarcalendar, openclaw CLI, jq) and the script's behavior (creating cron tasks, computing lunar→solar conversion) are consistent. Minor mismatch: SKILL.md says the script will call Python/lunarcalendar but the script hardcodes /tmp/lunar-venv/bin/python3 (a specific venv path) which SKILL.md does not describe.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The script creates a 'deletion' one-shot task whose message body is the literal text "openclaw cron rm <main_id>". That relies on some consumer (an agent or bot) executing command text posted as a message later; this behavior is not documented and expands the agent's effective scope (scheduling a future message that may be interpreted as an executable command). The script also assumes existence of /tmp/lunar-venv and jq/openclaw on PATH; SKILL.md doesn't instruct creation of that venv. These are surprising and could lead to unintended command execution or visible leaking of commands to channels/recipients.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec (instruction-only + a script). Nothing is downloaded or written by an installer. This is the lower-risk model for install mechanics.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables or external credentials are requested, which is proportionate. However the script invokes the openclaw CLI (and jq) and therefore implicitly relies on whatever credentials/config the CLI uses; those implicit credentials are not declared in the skill metadata and should be noted by users.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not modify other skills or global agent configuration. It only schedules cron tasks via the openclaw CLI, which is expected behavior for a scheduling helper.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing or running: 1) Confirm openclaw CLI and jq are present and that the CLI runs under the identity you expect (the script will create and remove cron jobs with that identity). 2) Ensure Python and the lunarcalendar library are available; the script calls /tmp/lunar-venv/bin/python3 — either create that venv with lunarcalendar or modify the script to use your Python. 3) Understand the deletion mechanism: the script schedules a future message whose content is the literal command "openclaw cron rm <id>"; verify whether your system will treat posted messages as executable commands (if it does, this will delete the job as intended; if it does not, the job may never be removed). 4) Consider privacy: the deletion command will be posted to the configured channel/target and may be visible to others. 5) If you need stronger guarantees, replace the 'post a message with a command' technique with a direct API/CLI-based scheduled deletion or an explicit scheduled job that calls the CLI on the host (not via a posted message). 6) Test in a safe environment first to confirm the deletion behavior and time calculations.
